name: React Frontend SPA
description: A React + Vite + TypeScript single-page application running on port 5173 that provides the task management UI. Communicates with the backend exclusively via HTTP REST API using VITE_API_URL env var (defaulting to http://localhost:8000). Structured across six modules: types.ts (canonical type mirrors), api.ts (typed fetch wrappers), App.tsx (state orchestration), TaskList.tsx, TaskItem.tsx (display + inline edit), TaskForm.tsx (create form). All files kept under 300 lines. No shared code with backend.

invariants: All backend communication is exclusively via HTTP REST through api.ts — no direct fetch calls from components
VITE_API_URL is the sole configuration point for backend URL; defaults to http://localhost:8000
No page reloads — all state mutations are SPA-style via React useState/useEffect (A11)
Empty description strings from the create form are sent as null to the backend (A12)
Task status badge colors are deterministic: pending=grey, in_progress=blue, done=green (AC15-AC16)
All non-ok HTTP responses are converted to ApiError with parsed detail before propagating to callers
TaskItem toggles between display mode and inline edit form mode — no separate edit page (AC18)
Delete success triggers immediate removal from local tasks state without waiting for re-fetch (AC19)
No code is shared between frontend and backend modules (AC26)
All source files are kept under 300 lines (AC25)
Local tasks state is the single source of truth for rendered UI — patched optimistically from mutation responses
The six prescribed modules are: types.ts, api.ts, App.tsx, TaskList.tsx, TaskItem.tsx, TaskForm.tsx

data_access.rationale: The frontend reads task data (id, title, description, status, created_at, updated_at) from the backend REST API for display in the task list UI. All task data is classified as PUBLIC — no PII or sensitive fields are involved. The frontend itself has no direct database access and performs no writes to any persistent store; all mutations are delegated to the backend via HTTP requests. The frontend reads VITE_API_URL from the environment at build/runtime to configure the backend endpoint.

side_effects.rationale: GET /tasks and GET /health fetch public task data and health status from the backend API for UI rendering
POST /tasks sends user-entered task creation data to the backend for persistence
PUT /tasks/{id} sends user-modified task fields to the backend for update
DELETE /tasks/{id} requests task removal from the backend by task identifier
